### Investment Memo: APP (AppLovin Corp.) — 16 October 2026

**Verdict**: BUY (staged initiation — starter position only) | Conviction: **Medium** (High on the business, Low on the next six weeks)
**Price Target**: $345 (≈ +30% from $266.13); bear/bull range $175–$470
**Time Horizon**: 12–24 months

---

**Investment Thesis**

AppLovin is a genuinely exceptional economic machine — 88% gross margins, ~77% operating margins, 73% ROIC, 102% FCF conversion, effectively zero net leverage — trading at ~17x FY26E earnings and a 5% FCF yield after a 64% drawdown. Forensic review **refutes the fraud thesis** (Beneish −2.52, negative accruals three years running, OCF/NI 1.19x, receivables growing slower than revenue), which removes the fat left tail. What remains is a legitimate but already largely priced debate about margin *duration*, sitting alongside a correlated legal overhang (SEC probe, securities class action, Dutch GDPR action — all one fact pattern: how AXON sources data) and the most hostile macro regime possible for a 2.2-beta, 76%-vol equity. The discount is real but not yet wide enough for full size.

---

**Key Findings by Domain**

- **Macro & Sector**: *Unfavourable / Neutral.* Fed restarted hiking (3.75–4.00%, dot 4.00–4.25%), 10Y at 5.10% and bear-steepening — every +25bp on the long end ≈ 3–5% de-rating on this duration profile; the Dec FOMC is the key macro date. Sector: independent adtech grows ~7% median with share leaking to Meta/Google, but APP is the dominant operator in the AI-performance niche (grows ~10x peer median, ~7x peer operating margin).
- **Geopolitical & Legal**: **HIGH.** Active SEC probe (whistleblower-originated, data provenance / platform ToS); class action *Talbot v. AppLovin* with **lead-plaintiff deadline 16 Nov 2026**; Dutch children's-privacy action (May 2026). All three trace to a single point of failure. US 51.6% / non-US 48.4% revenue; China-linked advertiser demand (Temu/Shein) remains ~30% below pre-tariff baselines.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Value**: FV ~$345 (range $240–440); at $266 the 23% discount sits below the 30% margin-of-safety bar for this risk profile — **buy threshold $242**. Financial quality 9/10; TTM owner earnings ~$4.5B; net debt/EBITDA 0.08x. Knock: $3.7B of buybacks executed at ~$450–500.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Growth**: **BUY** (not Strong). FY26E +48% revenue, Rule of 40 = 142, PEG ≈ 0.4. But sequential growth collapsed (+18.0% → +11.1% → +4.4%), the 7-quarter beat streak broke in Q2'26, and the entire re-rating depends on e-commerce/self-serve, where product-market fit is unproven. Sell-side revisions are unambiguously negative.
- **Quantitative Signals**: **Neutral/cautious.** Quality best-in-cohort (1 of 5); momentum and low-vol worst-in-cohort (5 of 5); −40.8% 12-1 momentum, decline still accelerating (−18.5% 1-mo), no basing pattern. Signature of multiple compression, not fundamental decay — but no quant evidence of a floor.
- **Financial Risk**: Credit/liquidity **LOW** (BBB+, 26.4x coverage, Z-score 3.74, F-score 9/9, no maturities before 2029); market risk **CRITICAL** (82% vol, realized −64% drawdown, five >12% single-day moves in nine months). Watch item: Q2 cash conversion 0.69x, DSO 103 days.
- **Non-Financial Risk**: **HIGH.** >$280M open-market insider sales, **zero** buys in 12 months; CEO sold ~$51M at ~$490 inside the eventual class period; CTO stepped down and CLO retired *mid-probe*; 87% founder voting control; officer exculpation adopted while under investigation.
- **ESG**: ESG Risk (below laggard). Governance 3/10; ~85% of the ESG risk is governance/product-integrity — the ESG risk *is* the investment risk. Environmental negligible.
- **Alternative Data**: Neutral with a contrarian-positive demand tilt. Advertiser spend at all-time highs (+28% vs Q4'25), e-commerce wallet share 8.1% (+140bp YoY), Q3 checks steady; but alt data is **blind to the one variable that matters** — AXON model-improvement cadence. Retail attention at 12-month lows (capitulation tell).
- **Short / Contrarian View**: Accounting short is **dead** (clean forensics across every test). The live thesis is margin-duration: R&D +127% YoY, first-ever guided EBITDA-margin decline (84%→83%), structural under-investment (R&D ~5% of revenue) vs. the "proprietary AI" narrative, DSO inflecting up. Consensus already models a plateau (2029E EPS +2.9%).

---

**Bull Case**
- 73% ROIC, 84% EBITDA margins and ~$4.5B TTM FCF at ~17x forward earnings / 5% FCF yield — a growth multiple that has round-tripped to a value multiple while the business still compounds ~30%+.
- Self-serve (opened June 2026) + e-commerce expand TAM from ~$10B mobile gaming to a $100B+ performance-ad pool; alt data confirms record advertiser demand and rising wallet share into Q4.
- Forensically clean accounting + fortress balance sheet (0.08x net leverage) + Q3 guide implying sequential *re*acceleration (+7.8%) — a clean 4-Nov print re-rates the stock violently given beta and positioning capitulation.

**Bear Case**
- Growth is hostage to AXON release cadence: one "lighter than normal" quarter already cost ~20% of market cap; R&D +127% and the first margin guide-down suggest the arbitrage is getting more expensive to defend against Meta/Google's superior first-party data.
- Correlated legal risk with dated catalysts: SEC enforcement (40–50% probability within 24 months per Geo-Legal) or platform-partner ToS enforcement would impair the core data flywheel — binary and undiversifiable.
- Macro duration trap: Fed hiking into 4.5–6% annualised CPI momentum with the 10Y at 5.10%; a 5.50% 10Y implies a further ~10–15% de-rating regardless of fundamentals.

**Key Risks**
1. SEC Wells notice / platform-partner (Apple, Meta, Google) enforcement of attribution terms — *thesis-level; exit trigger*.
2. Margin-duration break: two consecutive quarters of EBITDA-margin guide-downs with sequential growth <5%.
3. Earnings-quality drift: cash conversion <0.80x or DSO >110 days for two quarters (Q2 already printed 0.69x / 103d).
4. 4-Nov Q3 print: consensus sits at the *top* of guidance; Q2 precedent was −19.7% on a 1% miss.
5. Further C-suite turnover (CTO and CLO already gone mid-probe); EU injunction restricting profiling (~20%+ of revenue).

**Portfolio Construction Note**
**Initiate 1.0% now at $255–272; target 2.5%; hard cap 3.0%.** Tranche 2 (+0.75%) on a clean 4-Nov print (revenue ≥$2.075B, sequential ≥+7.5%, revisions stabilising); Tranche 3 (+0.75%) on either a pullback to $235–245 or SEC closure without action. Hard stop $195 (−27%; a tighter stop is noise at 4.8% daily σ). Do not chase above $300 pre-print. At 2.5%, beta-equivalent exposure is already ~5.4% — fund from an existing mega-cap ad/duration sleeve, not cash; cap at 2.0% if META/GOOGL/ad sleeves already exceed 10%. Trim one-third at $380–400; trim to a 1% core above $440.

---

**Dissent & data gaps flagged:** Agents genuinely split (Growth BUY / Value HOLD / Quant NEUTRAL / Short SHORT); the split resolves on (a) clean forensics removing the fraud tail and (b) the margin-of-safety bar not yet met for full size. Peer multiples rest on a 5-name hand-built cohort; country-level revenue is undisclosed (US/non-US only); SEC probe stage is press-reported, not 8-K-disclosed; 10-K/DEF 14A primary text was unavailable to three agents; settlement/damages figures are estimates.

---

## 2. Consensus Assessment: **SPLIT** — but a *resolvable* split

This is not the usual noise-around-a-mean dispersion. The agents cluster into three coherent and **mutually exclusive at this price** camps:

**Camp A — Own it for the machine (Growth, Value-to-a-point, Sector, Alt Data demand leg):** ~$4.5B TTM FCF, 73% ROIC, 84% EBITDA margins, 17x forward. The sell side is modelling a plateau (2029E EPS +2.9%) and the price has already discounted one.

**Camp B — Don't own it into a binary legal event at a hostile macro point (Geo Legal, Non-Fin, ESG, Macro, Short):** an active federal probe into the *data provenance* underpinning the 88% gross margin, a class action with a 16-Nov consolidation deadline, insider distribution with no bid, and a Fed that restarted hiking into a 76%-vol, β-2.16 equity.

**Camp C — Neutral on price action (Quant):** refuses both directions because momentum is worst-in-class and alpha is statistically insignificant (t ≈ −1.6, R² 0.138 — 86% idiosyncratic).

**How I resolve it:**

1. **The Short's fraud thesis is REFUTED — and this matters enormously.** Beneish −2.52, negative accruals three years running, OCF/NI 1.19x, AR growth (28.7%) far *below* revenue growth (70.0%), capex 0.5% of revenue. Four subsequent short reports have been followed by beats. **I remove the "accounting fraud" leg from the risk stack entirely.** This is the single largest piece of information in the entire packet, because it removes the fat left tail that would justify a pass.
2. **But the Short's *residual* thesis — margin duration — is validated by the bull camp's own data.** R&D +127% YoY, first-ever guided EBITDA margin *decline* (84% → 83%), sequentials 18.0 → 11.1 → 4.4. The growth camp reads these as "investment"; the bear reads them as "the margin line breaking last." Both are describing the same fact. I treat this as an **elevated but not thesis-breaking risk**, and size accordingly.
3. **Value's discipline outranks Growth's enthusiasm on price.** Growth is right about the three-year math; Value is right that a business whose revenue is hostage to a model-training cadence does not earn a 20% margin of safety. **Buy threshold $242, not $266.**
4. **Macro's duration math governs the timing, not the direction.** Every 25bp on the long end ≈ 3–5% on this name. A 10Y at 5.50% implies another 10–15% de-rating *all else equal*. This is the reason not to take a full position today.
5. **Legal's "correlated risks" finding is the key structural insight:** the SEC probe, the securities suit and the Dutch action are **one fact pattern** (how AXON sources data), not three diversifiable exposures. That is a genuine single point of failure and caps size regardless of how good the business is.

**Net conviction: MEDIUM-HIGH on the business, MEDIUM on the price, LOW on the next six weeks.** That is a starter position, not a target position.

---

## 3. Position Sizing Recommendation

### **Target weight 2.5% · Initiate 1.0% now · Hard cap 3.0%**

| Tranche | Size | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| **T1 — now** | **1.0%** | At market, $255–272 |
| **T2 — confirmation** | **+0.75%** | Q3 print (4-Nov-26): revenue ≥$2.075B, sequential growth ≥+7.5%, and FY26/FY27 EPS revisions stop falling |
| **T3 — price or clarity** | **+0.75%** | Either (a) pullback to $235–245 (Value's $242 threshold, ~15x FY26E, 5.6% FCF yield), or (b) SEC matter closed without enforcement |
| **Cap** | **3.0%** | Absolute — do not exceed even if all three legs trigger |

**Kelly logic.** Edge: FV $345 vs $266 = ~30% expected return on a ~23% MoS, but the distribution is wide ($175 bear → $470 bull). With win probability ~60% and a bear leg of −35%, full Kelly would imply a large allocation — **but full Kelly is inappropriate for a β-2.16, 76%-vol, single-point-of-failure name.** I apply a **one-third Kelly fractional** and then a hard risk-contribution cap.

**Risk-contribution math (why 3% and not 5%):**
- 2.5% × β 2.16 = **5.4% beta-equivalent** — already equivalent to a 5.4% position in a market-beta name.
- Position contribution to portfolio vol at 2.5%: 2.5% × 76.5% = **1.91% standalone**, ~0.92% portfolio-level given the 0.37 SPY correlation — acceptable, but only at starter size.
- At 5% (the "high-conviction" band), standalone vol contribution is 3.8% and a repeat of the realized −64% drawdown costs **320bp of portfolio** — an unacceptable single-name loss for a name carrying an unresolved federal probe. **That is the binding constraint, not valuation.**

**Why not zero / why not wait for $242:** the Value camp's threshold sits only 9% below spot on a stock that moves ±4.8% daily. Waiting has a real cost: the Alt Data demand leg (record advertiser spend, +140bp e-comm wallet share) and the 7/7→Q2 break pattern suggest the Q3 bar is achievable, and a clean print at 17x forward gaps this away. A 1% starter buys information and thesis-tracking at a trivially small portfolio risk.

---

## 4. Portfolio Fit Analysis

**Correlation (252d, my own calc) — the genuinely good news:**

| | APP | META | GOOGL | TTD | MSFT | SPY |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **APP** | 1.00 | **0.34** | **0.23** | **0.28** | **0.27** | **0.37** |

APP's correlation to every likely existing holding is **low (0.23–0.34)** despite a β of 2.16. R² vs SPY is only 0.138 — **86% of APP's variance is idiosyncratic.** Practically: APP is a *poor* diversifier of beta but an *excellent* diversifier of risk. It does not double up existing META/GOOGL/MSFT exposure the way a naive "another tech name" read would suggest.

**Sector/thematic concentration — where I *do* apply a haircut:**
- Correlation of *returns* is low, but **correlation of *drivers* is high**: APP's revenue is performance-ad budgets, the same pool that funds META and GOOGL. In an ad-recession or a privacy regime change, all three fall together even if daily correlation is 0.3.
- **If the portfolio already holds META + GOOGL + a digital-advertising thematic sleeve ≥10%, cap APP at 2.0%, not 3.0%.** I would fund T1 by trimming an existing mega-cap ad/platform position, not from cash — the *factor* exposure being added is idiosyncratic duration, not advertising beta.

**Factor exposure — net additive in three places, negative in two:**
| Factor | Effect | Action |
|---|---|---|
| **Quality (ROIC 73%, F-Score 9/9)** | Strongly **+** | Desirable — increases portfolio quality tilt |
| **Momentum (−40.8% 12-1)** | Strongly **−** | Must be offset: do **not** run this alongside an existing negative-momentum sleeve without netting |
| **Beta / duration (2.16)** | **−** | In a Fed-hiking regime this is the wrong factor. Cap size; monitor total portfolio beta |
| **Size / liquidity ($1.2B ADV)** | Neutral-+ | No liquidity constraint; institutional entry/exit unconstrained |
| **Value (17x fwd, 5% FCF yield)** | **+** | Genuine value leg |

**The unintended-tilt warning:** APP increases portfolio *duration* precisely when Macro says duration is the punished factor. If the portfolio is already long AI/long-duration growth, **fund APP from that sleeve, not from cash** — otherwise total portfolio rate sensitivity rises at the worst point in the cycle.

---

## 5. Entry Strategy: **Stage-in — do not buy all at once**

**Why not all at once:** two hard-dated catalysts inside 30 days, both two-sided, both with asymmetric downside.

| Date | Event | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| **4-Nov-26** | Q3 earnings | Consensus $2.0756B / $4.04 sits at the **upper end** of guide ($2.055–2.085B) — the sandbag is gone. Q2 precedent: a **1% revenue miss produced −19.7% in one day**. Binary. |
| **16-Nov-26** | Class action lead-plaintiff deadline | Expect a news-flow peak; consolidated complaint will likely name CEO/CFO individually and fold in the SEC probe |

Buying 2.5% on 16-Oct means carrying full size through a 19% gap risk twelve trading days out. Buying 1.0% means the same gap costs **26bp of portfolio** — recoverable. That asymmetry is the whole argument for staging.

**Execution notes:**
- T1 in **two clips** over 2–3 sessions; use limit orders — daily σ is 4.8%, so never market-buy at the open.
- **Do not chase above $300 pre-print.** Above $300 (≈17.8x FY26E → 19.5x) the MoS falls below 15% and the risk/reward inverts.
- Keep T3 dry powder. Given 76% vol, a retest of $235–245 has roughly a coin-flip probability within two quarters — either that, or legal clarity, will likely offer a better second entry than today's price.

---

## 6. Risk Management Rules

**Stop-loss: $195 hard (−27%).**
Not tighter. At 76.5% annualised vol, daily σ ≈ 4.8%; a 15–20% stop would be triggered by ordinary noise (the stock has had five >12% single-day moves in nine months, two of them **up**). $195 also sits below the 52-week low ($260.59) and below the −40% revenue-shock valuation implied by Fin Risk's stress case. A close below $195 on volume invalidates the "23% discount to FV" premise and the position should be exited, not averaged.

**Fundamental thesis-invalidation triggers — exit regardless of price:**
1. **SEC issues a Wells notice or formal enforcement action** on data-collection / platform-partner agreements. This is the binary tail. *Exit fully.*
2. **Any platform partner (Apple, Meta, Google) publicly enforces attribution or SDK terms against APP.** This converts a regulatory question into immediate product impairment — the single most damaging structural outcome.
3. **Two further consecutive quarters of EBITDA margin guide-downs** *with* sequential growth below +5%. That confirms the margin-duration short thesis (84% is rent on an arbitrage, not a software margin) and breaks the FV math.
4. **Cash conversion below 0.80x for two consecutive quarters, or DSO above 110 days.** Q2 already printed 0.69x and 103 days. One quarter is timing; two is a trend.
5. **Any further CTO/CFO/CLO departure.** Two of the three executives needed for the defense have already turned over mid-probe.
6. **Dutch GDPR action produces an injunction restricting profiling in the EU** (~20%+ of revenue).

**Trim triggers:**
- **$380–400** (Quant's 200-day reclaim area): trim one-third. Thesis is now consensus.
- **$440+** (top of Value's range, ~28x FY26E): trim to a core 1.0% residual. Above this you are paying for the optimistic DCF case, which requires 30% growth for five years *and* a legal all-clear.
- **Position drift >4.0% of portfolio** from appreciation: mechanical trim to 3.0%.

**Portfolio-level monitors:** total portfolio beta; aggregate AI/duration sleeve weight; monthly check that the 4-Nov print did not produce a fundamental (vs price) deterioration.

---

## 7. Final Portfolio Action: **INITIATE (starter position, scale-in)**

**Buy 1.0% of portfolio now at $255–272. Target 2.5%. Hard cap 3.0%. Staged entry across three tranches gated on the 4-Nov earnings print, a $235–245 pullback, or legal clarity.**

**One-line rationale:** Twelve specialists produced a genuinely split verdict, but the split resolves cleanly once you separate the *angle* of attack from the *quality* of the asset — the forensic short case is dead (Beneish −2.52, negative accruals, 1.19x cash conversion, zero asset-backed manipulation), leaving an exceptional business at 17x forward with a 5% FCF yield and a 23% discount to a $345 fair value, against a *known and dated* set of event risks (4-Nov print, 16-Nov lead-plaintiff deadline) and a macro regime hostile to 2.16-beta duration.

**You do not pass on a 73%-ROIC, 84%-EBITDA-margin franchise at 17x forward because of a legal overhang you cannot price — you size for it.** You also do not take 5% of it twelve trading days before a print that has historically gapped −19.7% on a 1% miss. One percent now, 2.5% on confirmation, and a $195 stop that caps the whole experiment at 26bp of portfolio downside. That is the correct expression of medium-high business conviction inside low near-term conviction.

**What flips this to ADD (3.0% full):** clean Q3 with sequential reacceleration ≥+7.5% **and** FY26/FY27 revisions stabilizing; or SEC closure without action; or a pullback to ≤$242 with the thesis intact.

**What flips this to EXIT (0%):** a Wells notice, platform-partner enforcement, or two consecutive quarters of margin-guide-down plus sub-5% sequential growth.

---

**Data gaps I am carrying, stated honestly:** peer multiples (TTD 13.4x, ADBE 14.7x, CRM 30.9x, NOW 85.0x, per Quant) are from a 5-name hand-built cohort, and the sector-peer tool returns mega-cap semis for a software company — **APP's relative valuation is directionally, not precisely, established.** Country-level revenue split is undisclosed by the company (US 51.6% / "Non-US" 48.4% is the entire granularity), so EU and China-origin exposure are estimates. The SEC probe's stage is press-reported only — no 8-K materiality disclosure exists. 10-K/DEF 14A text was unavailable to three separate agents, so governance and risk-factor detail is reconstructed from proxies and secondary reporting. Settlement/damages figures are analyst estimates, not company accruals.

## 1. Sector Overview

AppLovin competes in **digital advertising infrastructure** — the intermediary layer (ad networks, DSPs, SSPs, exchanges, measurement) sitting between advertisers and app publishers. The addressable market is large but structurally slowing: global ad spend is forecast +5.0% in 2026, internet advertising ~+9% CAGR (PwC, to ~$724B in 2026), and mobile absorbs ~74% of digital spend (>$430B in 2026). Sampled peer revenue totalled ~$7.1B against ~$604B at just two walled-garden platforms: the independent layer is ~1% of the pool and is being out-invested on AI and signal. The sector is **mature/late-cycle on volume growth but early-cycle on AI-driven creative/attribution**, which is precisely the pocket AppLovin monetises.

## 2. Key Tailwinds

- **Performance/e-commerce budget migration into mobile ad networks.** AppLovin reports e-commerce advertiser spend running **+28% vs Q4-2025** even in a seasonally soft quarter, and opened self-serve Ads Manager to all advertisers in late June 2026 — expanding TAM from gaming studios to SMB/mid-market DTC brands (a $400B+ pool it barely touched in 2024).
- **Signal-loss tailwind for AI networks.** Post-ATT privacy constraints (including the 2026 EU antitrust reshaping of Apple's prompt) degrade deterministic tracking, structurally favouring probabilistic, model-based attribution systems like AXON over cookie/ID-dependent intermediaries.
- **Operating leverage is extreme and intact.** APP's Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA margin was **83.9%** ($1.61B) on $1.92B revenue — incremental revenue drops through at ~80%+, so even decelerating growth still compounds cash. Peer-adjusted, no adtech at scale earns >41% operating margin.

- **Growth deceleration + guidance credibility.** Revenue growth has gone 75% (FY24) → 70% (FY25) → +53% (Q2-26, a *miss* vs own guidance) → Q3-26 guide $2.055–2.085B (~+45–48% YoY, below consensus on both revenue and EBITDA). ## 1. Business Quality Assessment — Moat Rating: **NARROW** (widening operationally, but unproven durability)

AppLovin is now, after the 2025 divestiture of its mobile-gaming studio portfolio, a **pure-play advertising technology company**. Its asset is AXON (rebranded AppLovin Ads in 2026): a machine-learning recommendation engine that bids for ad inventory across ~1bn+ daily mobile users, predominantly inside mobile games, and matches it against advertiser demand — increasingly e-commerce/DTC brands, not just game publishers.

**Evidence of a real moat:**
- **Cost/scale advantage in a two-sided auction.** More advertisers → better yield per impression → more publishers → more inventory. This is a genuine network effect, though a *local* one (it does not extend to social or search).
- **Extraordinary capital efficiency.** FY25 ROIC of **73%** (up from 41% in FY24, 17% in FY23) against a ~12% cost of capital. Capex is essentially nil ($28M in FY25 on $5.5B of revenue). This is software-margin economics on an ad-network revenue base.
- **Margin expansion is real and steep.** Gross margin 55.4% (2022) → 80.6% (2023) → 83.9% (2024) → **87.9% (2025)**; Q2'26 gross margin 88.3%, adjusted EBITDA margin **83.9%**, net margin 65.8%. Very few businesses in any industry earn 84% EBITDA margins.
- **Switching costs are moderate for publishers** (MAX mediation integration) but **low for advertisers** — a budget can be moved in a day. That asymmetry is the core weakness of the moat.

**Evidence the moat is not "Wide":**
- **Growth is a function of model iteration, not recurring contracts.** In Q2'26 the company missed its own guidance because "AXON model improvements moved slower than projected" during an architecture upgrade. A business whose growth rate can be set back by one quarter's model-training cadence does not have the predictability of a classic wide-moat franchise. Q2'26 revenue of $1.924B (+53% y/y, +4.4% q/q) was ~$20M below consensus; Q3'26 guidance of ~$2.07B also came in light.
- **Competitive intensity is the highest in the world.** AXON must out-predict Meta Advantage+, Google, Amazon and TikTok for conversion credit. These are vastly larger companies with first-party data that AppLovin does not have. Its edge is narrower inventory (mobile games) and a cheaper auction — not proprietary demand data.
- **Revenue quality is contested.** 2025–26 short-seller reports (Muddy Waters, Culper, and a January 2026 report) alleged attribution/ad-stacking improprieties and, in one case, money laundering; the SEC reportedly opened a probe (Oct 2025) into data-collection and ad-targeting practices. Management denies wrongdoing. I cannot independently verify the allegations — but in a business where the product *is* measurement, even an unproven allegation of measurement inflation is a genuine threat to the moat, because advertiser trust is the asset.

**Verdict on moat:** Narrow, and *directionally widening* on economics (margins, ROIC) while *directionally unproven* on durability. This is a superb business model with a single point of failure: continued algorithmic superiority.
